newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU tells France to stop attacks on Spanish produce.
newsitem.headline: EU tells France to stop attacks on Spanish produce.

text.p: French farmers' attacks on Spanish truckers importing vegetables and fruit to France are illegal, the European Commission said on Friday, and demanded Paris take action.
It accused French police of failing to take strong enough action to end what it called the farmers' "unacceptable behaviour".
"The Commission considers that these actions are illegal and that action should be taken under French law," the European Union executive said in a statement.
"The Commission expects that the French authorities will adopt urgently adequate and efficient meaasures to ensure order."
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler and Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti had written to the French government demanding it intervene.
Earlier this week, Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes rejected demands from angry Spanish farmers for a boycott of French products in reprisal for the attacks.

The boycott followed a week in which French farmers repeatedly dumped and destroyed Spanish produce arriving by truck or already stored in warehouses. The French farmers want tighter controls on cheaper imported vegetables and fruits.
Matutes said at the weekend that he had demanded "severe sanctions" from the EU to punish France for Spanish farmers' losses.
Spain has accused French police of standing by passively while the attacks went on. France apologised last week and promised to take action to prevent further attacks.
